figures.title: Aligned rounding errors add linearly; independent errors add in quadrature
figures.caption: With N = 4,096 terms, a half-step of 0.067, and an input RMS of 0.5, aligned errors would add to 4,096 × 0.0335 = 137.2. Independent errors add in quadrature: the worst case is √4,096 × 0.0335 = 2.14, and uniform rounding gives a per-term standard deviation of (step/√12) × x_rms ≈ 0.0192, so √4,096 × 0.0192 ≈ 1.23. The ratio between the linear and quadrature totals is 64, the square root of N.
figures.alt: Three horizontal bars. The aligned-error bar is 137.2 and fills the plot. The independent worst case is 2.14, and the uniform-rounding estimate is 1.23; both are short bars, roughly one sixty-fourth of the first. The caption gives the arithmetic: 4,096 × 0.0335, √4,096 × 0.0335, and √4,096 × 0.0192.

data.note: The ratio is 64 = √4,096. Aligned errors share a sign; independent errors cancel in quadrature.

figures.title: Group size and bit width set the rounding floor
figures.caption: A symmetric four-bit group with m = 4.0 has step 2·4/15 ≈ 0.533, so 0.1, 0.2, and 0.3 all round to 0.2667. Put 4.0 in its own group and the remaining weights get m = 0.3 and step 0.04, so 0.1, 0.2, and 0.3 land on distinct levels. The floor is set by the bit width: at four bits the step is m/7 and the half-step ≈ 0.2σ; at three bits the step is m/3 and the half-step ≈ 0.43σ; at two bits the step is m and the half-step ≈ 1σ. Smaller groups isolate outliers, at the cost of more scale metadata.
figures.alt: Three aligned panels. The first has one group containing 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, and 4.0, with m = 4.0 and step 0.533; the three small weights all round to 0.2667. The second puts 4.0 alone and gives the remaining group m = 0.3 and step 0.04, so 0.1, 0.2, and 0.3 land on distinct levels. The third gives the step and half-step at four, three, and two bits: step m/7 with half-step ≈ 0.2σ, step m/3 with half-step ≈ 0.43σ, and step m with half-step ≈ 1σ, so four bits is close to the floor.
